decision.trend: Research has been focused on understanding the properties of high-entropy alloys, including their magnetic properties, thermal conductivity, and microstructure. Recent studies have explored the effects of chemical short-range order and the formation of ordered clusters on the lattice thermal conductivity of refractory high-entropy alloys. Additionally, the magnetic properties of as-cast high-entropy alloys have been investigated, revealing multiple ferromagnetic transitions and high coercive fields.
decision.unsolved: The exact mechanisms behind the high coercive fields and the relationship between chemical short-range order and thermal conductivity are not yet fully understood. Further research is needed to elucidate the underlying physics and to optimize the properties of high-entropy alloys for various applications.
decision.lever: molecular dynamics simulations with varying chemical short-range order
decision.why: To further investigate the relationship between chemical short-range order and thermal conductivity, and to explore the potential for optimizing the properties of high-entropy alloys through tailored microstructure design.
